svg.title: BranchBook in AWS
svg.desc: What BranchBook has in AWS: the pipeline's release record and the hosted demo at branchbook.click, all built. Outside AWS, on the left: the Administrator, IAM user branchbook-admin, who signs in with aws login and gets short-lived credentials; GitHub, repository KatlehoKomeke/Appointment-Booking-System, with the environment aws-demo (main and v* tags only, no reviewers) holding the secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, the workflows deploy.yml (every push to main) and aws-connection-check.yml (manual), and infra.yml, which runs the tests and synth with no AWS access; a reviewer's browser, which needs no sign-in; and the administrator's machine, which runs cdk deploy by hand and builds the ARM64 image for ECR. The AWS account, whose ID is never committed, costs about $82 a month before VAT while the demo runs, inside the $90 budget; the domain costs about $3 a year. In us-east-1 (N. Virginia), built: the stack BranchbookAccount, deployed by hand by the administrator, holds the IAM OIDC provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com with audience sts.amazonaws.com; the AWS Budgets budget branchbook-monthly, $90 a month, which e-mails at $45, $72 and $90; the IAM role branchbook-github-deploy, with sessions of at most 1 hour, whose ARN is the stack output DeployRoleArn, copied once into the secret and never printed; and the IAM policy on that role, which allows only the statements AssumeCdkBootstrapRolesOnly and ReadReleaseRecordOnly. Beside it is the CDK bootstrap stack CDKToolkit, qualifier hnb659fds, with its roles, assets bucket and ECR repository. IAM and Budgets are global; no customer data is held here. In af-south-1 (Cape Town), built: a second CDKToolkit, with the five bootstrap roles deploy, lookup, cfn-exec, file-publishing and image-publishing, an assets bucket and an ECR repository, which holds the app image; the stack BranchbookRelease, deployed by the pipeline, holding the SSM parameter /branchbook/release, Standard tier, which records the last commit the pipeline deployed; and the hosted demo's two stacks, both deployed by the administrator by hand. BranchbookApp holds a Route 53 A alias record for branchbook.click, whose hosted zone Route 53 created when the domain was registered, so there is no DNS stack; AWS WAF, attached to the load balancer, which blocks /actuator with 403, allows 30 booking POSTs to /api/v1/appointments per address in 5 minutes, and applies the AWS managed rule groups for IP reputation, known bad inputs and common threats, with no sign-in; an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, HTTPS on 443 with an ACM certificate validated through Route 53 and the recommended TLS 1.3 policy, plain HTTP on 80 redirected to HTTPS, and invalid header fields dropped; CloudWatch and SNS: the log group /branchbook/app kept 7 days, and 3 alarms (5xx answers, no healthy task, less than 2 GB of database storage) sent to an SNS topic; and one ECS Fargate task, ARM64, 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB, in a public subnet with a public IP and no NAT, reachable only from the load balancer, with the simulated inbox switched off and a deployment circuit breaker that rolls back. BranchbookData holds a VPC, 10.40.0.0/16 across af-south-1a and af-south-1b, with a public and an isolated /24 subnet in each and no NAT gateway; Secrets Manager, holding the generated database credentials branchbook/database, which the task reads as DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD; and RDS for PostgreSQL 17, Single-AZ on db.t4g.micro in the isolated subnets, with 20 GB of gp3 storage growing to 50, encrypted, 7-day backups, TLS required and a final snapshot on deletion; PostgreSQL's own log is not exported, because it can quote a mobile number. Step A, twice: the administrator runs cdk deploy by hand, for BranchbookAccount in us-east-1, and for BranchbookData and BranchbookApp in af-south-1, which also pushes the image to the bootstrap ECR repository; the pipeline deploys none of these. Step 1: the deploy job in deploy.yml enters the environment aws-demo and signs in through OpenID Connect via AWS STS as the deploy role, with no stored keys. Step 2: the role assumes the af-south-1 bootstrap roles. Step 3: CloudFormation updates BranchbookRelease. Step 4: the job reads /branchbook/release back and fails unless it equals GITHUB_SHA. The main path is a reviewer's request: from the browser over HTTPS to Route 53, AWS WAF, the load balancer, the Fargate task on port 8080, health-checked at /readyz, and RDS on port 5432 over TLS, with no RDS Proxy.

g.text: Demo: about $82 a month before VAT; budget $90
